case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread concerns a company replacing an end-of-life BLE module with a different BLE module while keeping the same end product branding and model family. The customer correctly anticipates that the Bluetooth SIG qualification must be handled as a new registration rather than a simple update. The consultant provides pricing, manages qualification fee payment logistics, collects qualification inputs, and prepares the compliance documentation package. The discussion then progresses through registration preparation, review-page verification, and clarification of qualification system details before final submission.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The central qualification issue is that changing the BLE module requires a new Bluetooth SIG qualification submission despite the end product name remaining unchanged. The consultant explains that a new registration requires at least one model to be listed initially, while additional product variants can typically be added afterward through the Product List process. The customer is instructed to provide qualification input information and compliance-folder evidence, including Bluetooth-related user documentation, block diagrams, product drawings, and antenna performance documentation. The thread also discusses Review Page validation, public listing visibility, Test Coverage Waiver (TCW) concepts, and member-account data fields that are automatically sourced from the Bluetooth SIG membership database.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The consultant's reasoning is that a BLE module replacement changes the qualified Bluetooth design basis and therefore cannot simply reuse the previous product registration unchanged. The proper path is to create a new qualification submission, complete the required registration workflow, prepare supporting compliance-folder evidence, and then manage additional product listings after the initial qualification is established. Administrative details such as fee payment, review-page validation, and member-record accuracy are handled separately from the technical qualification decision.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: If the module replacement were treated as an existing qualification without completing the required new registration process, the product could be improperly listed and fail to satisfy Bluetooth SIG qualification requirements. Incorrect Product List entries could also create administrative correction work because erroneous model entries require deletion requests. Delays in obtaining required qualification inputs or compliance-folder materials could postpone qualification completion and product release schedules.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a qualified product changes to a different BLE module, do not assume the existing Bluetooth qualification remains valid simply because the product name or model family is unchanged. First determine whether the Bluetooth design basis has changed, then select the correct qualification path, collect compliance-folder evidence early, and complete the initial qualification before expanding product listings or variants.
